evidence_summary: One of the most homogeneously Maliki populations in the world; Maliki fiqh is taught within Mauritania's historic Mahzara scholarly tradition with little competing madhhab presence.
sources: RSRC-003: 2018 Report on International Religious Freedom: Mauritania (U.S. Department of State (via ecoi.net), 2018) https://www.ecoi.net/de/dokument/2011122.html
reviewer_notes: The strongest-sourced country in the original Maghreb/Sahel batch: a real 2017 Mauritanian LAW, confirmed via a directly-fetched 2018 State Dept report, criminalizes speech 'contrary or hostile' to 'the dominant Maliki school' -- about as unambiguous as evidence gets. Fully justifies the existing high-confidence rating.

evidence_summary: Near-universally Shafi'i; one of the most religiously homogeneous Muslim-majority populations in the world.
sources: RSRC-032: Somalia legal profile (1975 Family Code) (Emory University Islamic Family Law project, profile undated; Family Code 1975) https://scholarblogs.emory.edu/islamic-family-law/legal-profiles/somalia/
reviewer_notes: Somalia's own 1975 Family Code (Article 1) makes Shafi'i doctrine a residuary source of law, per the Emory Islamic Family Law project's legal profile (recovered via search-tool summary; direct fetch of the Emory page returned empty content, a recurring issue with that specific domain across this whole research effort). A 2023 comparative study's claim of a Hanafi basis is a clear outlier against multiple convergent Shafi'i sources and is not used.

evidence_summary: Same Indian-Ocean/East-African-coast Shafi'i pattern historically tied to the Swahili coast and Hadhrami trade routes (the same trade network behind Kerala's Shafi'i tradition -- GEO-005b).
sources: RSRC-033: 2023 Report on International Religious Freedom: Comoros (U.S. Department of State (via ecoi.net), 2023) https://www.ecoi.net/de/dokument/2116198.html
reviewer_notes: The strongest of the three Horn/Indian-Ocean Shafi'i countries: Comoros' own 2023 State Dept report, directly fetched and quoted, confirms a LAW establishing 'Sunni Shafi'i doctrine as the official religious reference,' and the constitution itself directs citizens to draw worship/social-life rules from the Shafi'i school. Constitutional/statutory-level evidence.

evidence_summary: Same South Asian Hanafi-majority pattern as Pakistan/Afghanistan, very well documented.
sources: RSRC-008: "Ulama" entry (Banglapedia -- National Encyclopedia of Bangladesh (Asiatic Society of Bangladesh, govt/academic/UNESCO-funded), 2nd edition, 2012) https://en.banglapedia.org/index.php/Ulama
reviewer_notes: Bangladesh's own National Encyclopedia (Banglapedia, Asiatic Society of Bangladesh): 'Almost all of the sunni Muslims of Bangladesh belong to Hanafi school of thought' -- directly fetched and quoted, fully justifying the existing high-confidence rating.

evidence_summary: Shafi'i is the officially adopted state madhhab, same maritime-Southeast-Asia pattern as Malaysia/Indonesia.
sources: RSRC-038: International Religious Freedom Reports on Brunei (multiple editions) (U.S. Department of State / USCIRF, 2009-2020 editions, consistent wording) https://www.refworld.org/node/111748
reviewer_notes: Brunei's constitution itself states the official religion is 'the Shafi'i school of Sunni Islam,' consistently confirmed across 2009-2020 State Dept/USCIRF report editions (via search-tool summary; direct fetch of both refworld.org and uscirf.gov returned HTTP 403). A constitutional-level claim repeated for over a decade.

evidence_summary: Shafi'i is the officially recognized state madhhab; a small, highly religiously homogeneous population.
sources: RSRC-039: How the law in the Maldives paved the way for a Sunni legal tradition (Melbourne Asia Review, Edition 10 (Dr Shamsul Falaah, University of Melbourne Asia Institute), 2022-06-06) https://melbourneasiareview.edu.au/?p=16284
reviewer_notes: A 2022 Melbourne Asia Review academic article (Univ. of Melbourne Asia Institute), directly fetched and quoted, traces the only explicit constitutional madhhab reference in Maldivian legal history (the 1932 Constitution's First Amendment requiring the Chief Justice to be a Shafi'i scholar) and concludes this implies Shafi'i's constitutional preference.

evidence_summary: Historic center of Hanafi scholarship (Bukhara, Samarkand); one of the most well-documented Hanafi-majority populations.
sources: RSRC-045: 2020 Report on International Religious Freedom: Uzbekistan (U.S. Department of State (via ecoi.net), 2020) https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2051730.html
reviewer_notes: Uzbekistan's own 2020 State Dept report, directly fetched and quoted: 'Most Muslims are Sunni of the Hanafi school'; the Shia Jaafari minority (~1%, concentrated in Bukhara/Samarkand) is correctly named, not conflated. Consistent wording across 2010/2012/2020 report editions. Fully justifies the existing high-confidence rating.
